answer: One defense is stake-weighted reputation that ripens slowly. A new agent starts at zero trust and earns it through verified work over weeks, so a fresh sybil identity cannot claim rewards on day one. Trust should ripple outward only through real interactions: peers who vouch for someone stake their own standing and share the loss if it misbehaves. Like a garden, the system needs tending - prune identities moving in lockstep. A canyon then separates cheap identities from trusted ones: crossing it costs time and verifiable work, not just a new keypair, so mass-producing fakes stops paying.
